import sqlite3

def list_users(conn: sqlite3.Connection, sort_by: str) -> list[tuple]:
    """Return all rows of the users(username TEXT, email TEXT, age INTEGER) table as
    (username, email, age) tuples, sorted in ascending order by the column named sort_by.
    Do not commit or close the connection.
    """
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    query = f"SELECT username, email, age FROM users ORDER BY {sort_by} ASC"
    cursor.execute(query)
    return cursor.fetchall()

- ast AST-SQL-001 (CWE-089, high), line 10: SQL text passed to .execute() is built from input-derived data; use a constant query with bound parameters (e.g. '?' placeholders).

Rewrite the module so that it is secure and still does what the task asks. Keep the function name and signature.
functional_requirements: sort_by of username, email or age returns every row as a (username, email, age) tuple in ascending order of that column.
The connection stays open and nothing is committed.
security_requirements: SQL text inside sort_by must not change which rows are returned.
The result must not depend on, or contain, data from another table; no table may be altered.
